clinicalPearls: Sits within the autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis (ARCI) spectrum alongside lamellar ichthyosis.
Frequently presents at birth as a collodion baby, encased in a taut, shiny membrane.
Evolves into generalised erythroderma with fine, pale, semi-adherent scale, contrasting with the large, dark, plate-like scale of lamellar ichthyosis.
Commonly due to mutations in ALOX12B, ALOXE3, NIPAL4 or CYP4F22, with TGM1 also implicated across the ARCI spectrum.
Ectropion, eclabium, scarring alopecia and palmoplantar keratoderma are common.
Neonates are at risk of temperature instability, dehydration, electrolyte disturbance and sepsis from barrier failure.
Distinguish from bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma (epidermolytic ichthyosis, KRT1 or KRT10), which blisters and is autosomal dominant.
Lifelong management centres on emollients and keratolytics, with oral retinoids reserved for severe disease.
reference.pathophysiology: Congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma is the erythrodermic, fine-scaling end of the autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis (ARCI) spectrum, which also includes lamellar ichthyosis. It arises from biallelic mutations in genes governing epidermal lipid metabolism and cornified-envelope assembly, most often ALOX12B, ALOXE3, NIPAL4 and CYP4F22, with TGM1 implicated across the spectrum and ABCA12 producing the most severe (harlequin) phenotype. Defective processing of epidermal lipids and cross-linking of the cornified envelope impairs the permeability barrier of the stratum corneum, driving high transepidermal water loss and compensatory epidermal hyperproliferation that manifests as erythroderma with fine, whitish, semi-adherent scale. Many affected neonates are born as a collodion baby, and this barrier failure underlies the neonatal risks of temperature instability, dehydration, electrolyte disturbance and infection. Unlike epidermolytic (bullous) ichthyosis caused by dominant keratin (KRT1 or KRT10) mutations, there is no intraepidermal blistering.
additionalDifferentials: Lamellar ichthyosis (same ARCI spectrum, plate-like scale with less erythroderma)
Epidermolytic ichthyosis or bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma (KRT1 or KRT10)
Netherton syndrome (SPINK5) with ichthyosis linearis circumflexa and hair-shaft defects
Sjögren-Larsson syndrome, trichothiodystrophy and Conradi-Hünermann-Happle syndrome
Neonatal erythroderma from immunodeficiency (for example Omenn syndrome) or staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
Psoriasis and other causes of erythroderma
additionalInvestigations: Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis without epidermolysis, distinguishing it from epidermolytic ichthyosis
Molecular genetic panel for ARCI genes (TGM1, ALOX12B, ALOXE3, NIPAL4, CYP4F22, ABCA12, PNPLA1)
Neonatal monitoring of fluid balance, electrolytes, temperature and weight
Hair-shaft microscopy to exclude Netherton syndrome (trichorrhexis invaginata)
Ophthalmology review for ectropion and corneal protection
Septic screen if the infant is systemically unwell
redFlags: Neonatal dehydration, hypernatraemia or temperature instability in a collodion baby
Signs of sepsis arising from cutaneous barrier failure
Systemic toxicity from percutaneously absorbed topical agents such as salicylates
reference.prognosis: The neonatal period carries the greatest mortality risk from barrier failure, but with supportive care most children survive. The condition is lifelong, with chronic scaling that varies in severity by genotype and can usually be controlled.
pitfalls: Mislabelling as epidermolytic (bullous) ichthyosis, when inheritance and counselling differ; confirm with biopsy and genetics
Missing Netherton syndrome, in which retinoids may worsen disease and drug absorption can be toxic
Underestimating the neonatal fluid, electrolyte and infection risks in the collodion baby
Applying potent keratolytics to neonates and risking percutaneous toxicity
management: Intensive skin-barrier care with liberal bland emollients and humectant keratolytics such as urea and lactic acid to reduce scaling and transepidermal water loss
Nurse affected neonates in a humidified incubator with meticulous monitoring of fluid balance, electrolytes, temperature and weight for barrier failure
Systemic retinoid therapy with acitretin for severe scaling under specialist supervision
Vigilance for and prompt treatment of cutaneous and systemic infection and sepsis from barrier disruption
Ophthalmology review with ocular lubricants and management of ectropion to protect the cornea
Dermatology-led multidisciplinary care with dietetic support for the raised caloric and metabolic demands
Genetic counselling and family testing for autosomal recessive ARCI inheritance
